target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`currentProviders()` in the session upstream-activity monitor read the **mutable** `getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry` to discover session-catalog providers. A standalone plugin load/reload swaps `activeRegistry` (via `setActivePluginRegistry` → `syncTrackedSurface(state.sessionExtension, …)`), so the long-lived background monitor could observe a post-swap registry with no catalogs and silently stop watching upstream activity.

This is the same drift class fixed upstream in `session-catalog.ts`, which now reads the bootstrap-pinned `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the pinned session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()?.sessionCatalogs`) instead of the mutable `activeRegistry`. The monitor is a persistent loop with no request-scoped pin, so it must use the stable surface the gateway already pins at startup.

## User Impact

The upstream-activity monitor keeps watching the correct session catalogs across plugin-registry churn instead of observing an empty set. No config or protocol change; no migration.

## Evidence

- Regression test `session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts` "reads the pinned session-extension registry after active registry churn": pins a registry carrying the provider, swaps the mutable `activeRegistry` to an empty one, asserts the monitor still calls the pinned provider. **Red before the fix** (`checkUpstreamActivity` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.test.ts` → 1 + 17 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` still reads the mutable `activeRegistry` (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The upstream monitor (`src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts`) read the session-extension catalog from the wrong registry state accessor (`getPluginRegistryState().activeRegistry`), which did not reflect the pinned/active session-extension registry. It now reads via `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()` so `currentProviders()` returns the live session catalogs used for upstream activity probing.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The fix is exercised by the existing test suite which drives the real session state database (`openOpenClawStateDatabase`) against throwaway temp dirs and asserts monitor tick behavior end to end.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Observed result after fix: All 17 integration tests pass, covering upsert/read/watch of session upstream links, missing-counter accounting, and the monitor tick that consumes the active session-extension catalog providers. The change swaps the registry accessor to the pinned/active one without altering the provider-mapping logic, so the tick now sees the correct live catalogs.

What was not tested: Live multi-plugin gateway deployment against a real plugin registry was not run (no plugin fixtures beyond the in-test catalog providers). The in-repo integration suite exercises the exact changed code path (the registry accessor call inside `currentProviders()`) against the real state database.
